chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Isma'il al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

"Five [types of women] a man may divorce at any time: the pregnant one, the one with whom he has not had intercourse, the one whose husband is absent, the one who has not yet menstruated, and the one who has sat [waiting] for menstruation."
And whenever the man divorces her, it is a single divorce, and her waiting period is the bearing of the child in her womb. That to which this points is what he narrated:

key_terms.عَلَى كُلِّ حَالٍ: at any time / in any state
key_terms.لَمْ يُدْخَلْ بِهَا: he has not had intercourse with her
key_terms.وَضْعُ مَا فِي بَطْنِهَا: the bearing/delivery of what is in her womb

ai.seo_question: What are the five types of women a man can divorce at any time according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility of *talaq al-sunnah* (divorce during purity) by listing five categories of women eligible for immediate divorce, including the pregnant, the virgin, the absent wife, the pre-menarche girl, and the post-menstrual woman. It establishes that such a divorce is revocable (*raj'i*) and that the waiting period (*iddah*) for a pregnant woman concludes with childbirth, a principle derived from Quranic verse 65:4. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the husband's discretion in timing the divorce relative to the wife's physical state to ensure clarity in lineage and waiting periods.
